## Definitions

- [passage] - Indexes are not used for comparisons where the `let` operand resolves to an empty or missing value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#expr-in-lookup-operations · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, let
- [passage] The query does not return the array field (meaning the array is not included in the query projection). This means that to cover a query, the multikey index must be compound. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: index, projection
- [passage] - The query does not return the array field (meaning the array is not included in the query projection). This means that to cover a query, the multikey index must be [compound.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#std-label-compound_multikey_indexes) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#covered-queries · keywords: index, projection
- [passage] A query shape is a set of specifications that group similar queries together. Specifications can include filters, sorts, projections, aggregation pipeline stages, a namespace, and others. Queries that have similar specifications have the same query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: projection, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md
- [passage] For instance, the inequality operators $nin and $ne are not very selective since they often match a large portion of the index. As a result, in many cases, a $nin or $ne query with an index may perform no better than a $nin or $ne query that must scan all documents in a collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern
- [passage] Further optimization can occur if the regular expression is a "prefix expression", which means that all potential matches start with the same string. This allows MongoDB to construct a "range" from that prefix and only match values from the index within the specified range. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#case-sensitive-queries · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern
- [passage] A regular expression is a "prefix expression" if it starts with a caret (`^`) or a left anchor (`\A`), followed by a string of simple symbols. For example, the regex `/^abc.*/` is optimized to match only the values from the index that start with `abc`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#case-sensitive-queries · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, ) or a left anchor (, /^abc.*/, abc

- [passage] If `<value>` is a regular expression, MongoDB expands the statement to use the `$regex` operator `{ field: { $regex: <value> } }`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#match-a-regular-expression · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, <value>, $regex, { field: { $regex: <value> } }

## Structure and components

- [passage] When run on [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#std-program-mongos), indexes can only cover queries on [sharded](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-shard) collections if the index contains the shard key. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#sharded-collections · keywords: index, projection, sharded query targeting, mongos · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [fact] On sharded collections queried through mongos, an index covers a query only if it contains the shard key; the manual states an _id-only exception, but that exception is disputed (see disagreements). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, projection, sharded query targeting, Projection Optimization and Covered Query Design
- [passage] When an index [covers](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#std-label-indexes-covered-queries) a query, MongoDB can both match the query conditions **and** return the results using only the index keys. MongoDB does not need to examine documents from the collection to perform any part of the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#covered-queries · keywords: index, projection, query optimization
- [passage] Index filters are set with the [`planCacheSetFilter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/plancachesetfilter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.planCacheSetFilter) command and determine which indexes the planner evaluates for a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape). A plan cache query shape consists of a combination of query, sort, and projection specifications. If an index filter exists for a given query shape, the planner only considers those indexes specified in the filter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: index, projection, query shape, planCacheSetFilter
- [passage] If an array field contains multiple documents with the same field name and the [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) method includes a [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) on that repeating field, the returned documents may not reflect the sort order because the sort was applied to the elements of the array before the [`$`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/positional.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-) projection operator. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/positional.md#sorts-and-the-positional-operator · keywords: cursor, projection, find(), sort()
- [passage] The `$text` operator assigns a score to each result document. The score represents the relevance of a document to a given query. The score can be part of a [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) method specification as well as part of the projection expression. The `{ $meta: "textScore" }` expression provides information on the processing of the `$text` operation. See [`$meta`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-meta) projection operator for details on accessing the score for projection or sort. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#text-score · keywords: cursor, projection, $text, sort(), { $meta: "textScore" }, $meta

- [passage] `$ne` selects documents where the value of the field is not equal to the specified value. This includes documents that do not contain the field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/ne.md#definition · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $ne
- [passage] The following example returns movies where `runtime` is greater than `1000` minutes and `rated` is not equal to `"G"`. Because `$ne` also matches documents that don't contain the `rated` field, the query returns movies even when the rating data is unavailable: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/ne.md#match-document-fields-that-are-not-equal · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, runtime, 1000, rated, "G", $ne · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nin.md
- [passage] [`updateMany()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.updatemany.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.updateMany) also selects a document when the document does not contain the field [`$nin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nin.md#mongodb-query-op.-nin) is matching on. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nin.md#select-on-elements-not-in-an-array · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, updateMany(), $nin
- [passage] The `{ metacritic : { $exists: false } }` query matches documents that do not contain the `metacritic` field: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#existence-check · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, { metacritic : { $exists: false } }, metacritic
- [passage] The `{ item : { $exists: False } }` query matches documents that do not contain the `item` field: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#existence-check · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, { item : { $exists: False } }, item
- [passage] The `[ item => [ $exists => false ] ]` query matches documents that do not contain the `item` field: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#existence-check · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, [ item => [ $exists => false ] ], item
- [passage] The `{ item => { $exists => false } }` query matches documents that do not contain the `item` field: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#existence-check · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, { item => { $exists => false } }, item
- [passage] The `{ item, { $exists, BCON_BOOL (false) } }` query matches documents that do not contain the `item` field: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#existence-check · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, { item, { $exists, BCON_BOOL (false) } }, item
- [passage] The `bson.D{{"item", bson.D{{"$exists", false}}}}` query matches documents that do not contain the `item` field: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#existence-check · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, bson.D{{"item", bson.D{{"$exists", false}}}}, item
- [passage] If the `$regex` pattern doesn't contain an anchor, the pattern matches against the whole string. For example: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#multiline-match-for-lines-starting-with-specified-pattern · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $regex
- [passage] The following example uses the regular expression `"(?i)a(?-i)bc"` to match `sku` field strings that contain: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#use-a-regular-expression-to-match-case-in-strings · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, "(?i)a(?-i)bc", sku

## How it works

- [passage] Query optimization improves the efficiency of read operations by reducing the amount of data that query operations need to process. Use indexes, projections, and query limits to enhance query performance and reduce resource consumption. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, projection, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md
- [passage] Multikey indexes can cover queries over the non-array fields if the index tracks which field or fields cause the index to be multikey. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#multikey-covering · keywords: index, projection
- [passage] When an index covers a query, the explain result has an `IXSCAN` stage that is **not** a descendant of a `FETCH` stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#covered-queries · keywords: index, projection, IXSCAN, FETCH
- [fact] When $or clauses are equality checks on the same field, the MongoDB manual says to use $in instead; $in runs one IXSCAN in total, whereas $or runs one IXSCAN per condition. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or/ · keywords: $in, index, $in and $or Index Bounds and Union Plans
- [fact] A compound index often outperforms a union of single-field indexes for an $or with shared extra filters, because a union must merge and deduplicate results. This is asserted by a blog and a forum reply without a controlled benchmark. — https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-index-for-or-queries/view · keywords: $in, index, $in and $or Index Bounds and Union Plans
- [passage] If the collection has an index that includes the sort fields, MongoDB can use that index to obtain the results of a sort operation. In $or queries, MongoDB may use multiple indexes to support a single sort operation, because each clause of the $or expression can use its own index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/ · keywords: $in, index
- [passage] A covered query is a query that can be satisfied entirely using an index and doesn't have to examine any documents. An index covers a query when all of the following apply: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, projection · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md
- [passage] When executing $or queries with a sort(), MongoDB can use indexes that support the $or clauses. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or/ · keywords: $in, index
- [passage] `$in` compares each parameter to each document in the collection, which can cause performance issues. To improve performance, create an index on the `field` you want to query. An index allows MongoDB to create bounds for each `$in` element and search more efficiently. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#syntax · keywords: $in, index, field
- [passage] | Unique Index Key Pattern | Update Operation | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | `{ name : 1 }` | `db.people.updateOne( { name: "Andy" }, { $inc: { score: 1 } }, { upsert: true } )` | The `score` field of the matched document is incremented by 1. | | `{ name : 1 }` | `db.people.updateOne( { name: { $ne: "Joe" } }, { $set: { name: "Andy" } }, { upsert: true } )` | The operation fails because it modifies the field in the unique index key pattern (`name`). | | `{ name : 1 }` | `db.people.updateOne( { name: "Andy", email: "andy@xyz.com" }, { $set: { active: false } }, { upsert: true } )` | The operation fails because the equality predicate fields (`name`, `email`) do not match the index key field (`name`). | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findAndModify.md#upsert-with-unique-index · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, { name : 1 },  | The ,  field of the matched document is incremented by 1. | | ,  |  · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findAndModify.md
- [passage] When you use a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage it should typically be the last stage in your pipeline, used to specify which fields to return to the client. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#project-stage-placement · keywords: projection, $project
- [passage] Using a `$project` stage at the beginning or middle of a pipeline to reduce the number of fields passed to subsequent pipeline stages is unlikely to improve performance, because the database performs this optimization automatically. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#project-stage-placement · keywords: projection, $project
- [fact] $expr with non-JavaScript aggregation operators is faster than $where because it runs no JavaScript. If custom JavaScript is unavoidable, $function inside $expr is preferred over $where. $where does not work inside $elemMatch (top-level documents only). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)
- [passage] When an operation both sorts *and* [projects](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-projection) with the same fields, MongoDB sorts on the original field values before applying the projection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#interaction-with-projection · keywords: projection · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md
- [passage] The preceding examples return the documents that have a `zipcode` value of `"63109"`, but these documents include only the `_id` field because the projection operation found no matching elements. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch.md#elemmatch-https-www-mongodb-com-docs-manual-reference-operator-projection-elemmatch-md-mongodb-projection-proj-elemmatch-with-multiple-fields · keywords: projection, zipcode, "63109", _id
- [passage] When $in is used alone, it is an equality operator that performs a series of equality matches. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: $in · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md
- [passage] When you need a subset of fields from documents, you can improve performance by returning only the fields you need. Projections reduce network traffic and processing time. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: projection · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md
- [passage] The previous results are unexpected because none of the whole words in the returned `artist` fields begin with the matched string (`yster`). The `Ö` character in documents `_id: 0` and `_id: 1` is ignored when performing the match because `Ö` is a UTF-8 character. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#extend-regex-options-to-match-characters-outside-of-ascii · keywords: projection, artist, yster,  character in documents ,  and ,  is ignored when performing the match because 
- [passage] In this example, the $in array is truncated at the 376th element because the size of the command attribute would exceed maxLogSizeKB if it included the subsequent elements. The remainder of the command attribute is omitted. The truncated log entry resembles the following output: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: $in
- [passage] In this example, the `$in` array is truncated at the 376th element because the size of the `command` attribute would exceed [`maxLogSizeKB`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.maxLogSizeKB) if it included the subsequent elements. The remainder of the `command` attribute is omitted. The truncated log entry resembles the following output: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#truncation · keywords: $in, command, maxLogSizeKB
- [passage] The `$eq` operator is equivalent to the `{ field: <value> }` form, except when `<value>` is a regular expression. See below for [examples.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#std-label-eq-usage-examples) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#syntax · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $eq, { field: <value> }, <value>
- [passage] An explicit query that uses `$eq` and a regular expression only matches an object that is also a regular expression. The example query returns no results because values in the `company` field are strings. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#regex-match-behavior · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $eq, company
- [passage] The `$not` operator can yield unexpected results when used with an array. To match documents based on multiple false conditions, use [`$nor`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nor.md#mongodb-query-op.-nor) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/not.md#arrays · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $not, $nor · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/not/
- [passage] Some queries need to execute conditional logic when defining a query filter. The aggregation pipeline provides the [`$cond`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/cond.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-cond) operator to express conditional statements. By using `$expr` with the [`$cond`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/cond.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-cond) operator, you can specify a conditional filter for your query statement. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#use-expr-with-conditional-statements · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $cond, $expr
- [passage] Evaluates a boolean and returns the opposite boolean value; i.e. when passed an expression that evaluates to `true`, [`$not`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/not.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-not) returns `false`; when passed an expression that evaluates to `false`, [`$not`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/not.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-not) returns `true`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/not.md#definition · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, true, $not, false
- [passage] The counter for `$expr` increments when the query runs. The counter for `$gt` does not. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#metrics · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $expr, $gt
- [passage] When comparing arrays, `$ne` behaves differently depending on whether you pass a scalar or an array as the comparison value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/ne.md#arrays · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $ne
- [passage] The `{ $ne : null }` filter on a dotted path can match a document even when `{ path : { $exists: true } }` does not, when the path traverses an array. For details, see [Null Comparisons on Array Fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#std-label-null-semantics-arrays) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#non-equality-filter · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, { $ne : null }, { path : { $exists: true } }
- [passage] The previous query is invalid because it uses [`$ne`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/ne.md#mongodb-query-op.-ne) more than once on the `status` field at the same object level. Use [`$nin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nin.md#mongodb-query-op.-nin) instead: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#examples · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $ne, status, $nin
- [passage] Two similar comparisons are made in the [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match) stage. First the [`$year`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/year.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-year) and [`$month`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/month.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-month) operators extract the year and month, respectively, from the `logoutTime` Date object. Then the month and year are checked to see if they match the selection targets. Since "January" is encoded as "1", [`$expr`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#mongodb-query-op.-expr) is true when the year and month are equal ([`$eq`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/eq.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-eq)) to "2021" and "1". — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/dateSubtract.md#subtract-a-fixed-amount · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $match, $year, $month, logoutTime, $expr
- [passage] | Option | Description | | --- | --- | | `i` | Case insensitivity to match upper and lower cases. For an example, see [Perform Case-Insensitive Regular Expression Match.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#std-label-regex-case-insensitive) | | `m` | For patterns that include anchors (`^` for the start, `$` for the end), match at the beginning or end of each line for strings with multiline values. Without this option, these anchors match at beginning or end of the string. For an example, see [Multiline Match for Lines Starting with Specified Pattern.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#std-label-regex-multiline-match) If the pattern has no anchors or if the string value has no newline characters (for example, `\n`), the `m` option has no effect. | | `x` | "Extended" capability to ignore all white space characters in the `$regex` pattern unless escaped or included in a character class. Additionally, it ignores characters in-between and including an un-escaped hash/pound (`#`) character and the next new line, so that you may include comments in complicated patterns. This only applies to data characters; white space characters may never appear within special character sequences in a pattern. The `x` option does not affect the handling of the VT character (code 11). | | `s` | Allows the dot character (`.`) to match all characters *including* newline characters. For an example, see [Use the `.` Dot Character to Match New Line.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#std-label-regex-dot-new-line) | | `u` | Unicode option, which is accepted but redundant. UTF is enabled by default for `$regex`. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#syntax · keywords: query operator anti-pattern,  | For patterns that include anchors (,  for the start, , \n,  option has no effect. | | , $regex
- [passage] When specifying `*UCP` or any other regular expression option, use the correct escape characters for your shell or driver. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#extend-regex-options-to-match-characters-outside-of-ascii · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, *UCP

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] To include a regular expression in an `$in` query predicate operator, you can only use JavaScript regular expression objects (`/pattern/` ). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#in-expressions · keywords: $in, query operator anti-pattern, query shape, /pattern/
- [passage] To determine whether a query is a covered query, use the [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method. See [Covered Queries.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-output-covered-queries) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#explain-results · keywords: cursor, index, projection, db.collection.explain(), explain()
- [passage] To index fields in embedded documents, use [dot notation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-dot-notation). See [Create an Index on an Embedded Field.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-single/create-single-field-index.md#std-label-index-embedded-fields) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#embedded-documents · keywords: index, projection
- [passage] To learn how to use wildcard projection with a compound wildcard index to filter fields, see [Filter Fields with a `wildcardProjection`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound.md#std-label-wc-compound-index-wcProject) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-multiple-fields.md#learn-more · keywords: index, projection, wildcardProjection
- [passage] To achieve a covered query, you must index projected fields. The ESR (Equality, Sort, Range) rule applies to the order of fields in the index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, projection
- [passage] To determine whether a query is a covered query, use the db.collection.explain() or the explain() method. See Covered Queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, projection
- [passage] To achieve a covered query, you must index projected fields. The [ESR (Equality, Sort, Range) rule](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md#std-label-esr-indexing-guideline) applies to the order of fields in the index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#example · keywords: index, projection
- [passage] Use a Sparse Index to Improve $exists Performance — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists/ · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern
- [passage] To include [expressions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) in a query predicate, use the [`$expr`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#mongodb-query-op.-expr) operator. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#expressions-in-query-predicates · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, query shape, $expr · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/function.md
- [passage] To resolve, remove the component of the field path that follows the [`$`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/positional.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-) projection operator. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/positional.md#positional-operator-placement-restriction · keywords: projection · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] To perform an `$elemMatch` projection when using the .NET/C# driver, call the `ElemMatch()` method on the projection builder. Pass the name of the array field to project and the filter to apply to the array elements. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch.md#zipcode-search · keywords: projection, $elemMatch, ElemMatch()
- [passage] To match scalar values, use the equality operator along with the scalar value that you want to match (`{$eq: <scalar value>}`). For example, the following [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) operation queries for all documents where the value of the `zipcode` field is `"63109"`. The projection includes the matching element of the `athletics` array where the value is `basketball`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch.md#elemmatch-https-www-mongodb-com-docs-manual-reference-operator-projection-elemmatch-md-mongodb-projection-proj-elemmatch-with-multiple-fields · keywords: projection, {$eq: <scalar value>}, find(), zipcode, "63109", athletics
- [passage] To perform an `$elemMatch` operation against scalar values in an array when using the .NET/C# driver, call the `ElemMatch()` method on the projection builder. Pass the name of the array field to project and an equality filter for the field `"$eq"` and the value you want to compare against. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch.md#elemmatch-https-www-mongodb-com-docs-manual-reference-operator-projection-elemmatch-md-mongodb-projection-proj-elemmatch-with-multiple-fields · keywords: projection, $elemMatch, ElemMatch(), "$eq"
- [passage] To include the text search score by using the .NET/C# driver, call the [MetaTextScore()](https://mongodb.github.io/mongo-csharp-driver/3.11.0/api/MongoDB.Driver/MongoDB.Driver.ProjectionDefinitionBuilder-1.MetaTextScore.html) method on the projection builder. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#meta-indexkey · keywords: projection
- [passage] To return one document from a time series collection, you can use the `findOne()` method. The following example uses the `projection` field in the query to omit the `_id` field from the returned documents: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-procedures.md#query-a-time-series-collection · keywords: projection, findOne(), _id
- [passage] To return one document from a time series collection, you can use the [`db.collection.findOne()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findone.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.findOne) method. The following example uses the `projection` field in the query to omit the `_id` field from the returned documents: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-procedures.md#query-a-time-series-collection · keywords: projection, db.collection.findOne(), _id
- [passage] To specify a projection document, chain the [com.mongodb.client.FindIterable.projection](https://mongodb.github.io/mongo-java-driver/3.4/javadoc/com/mongodb/client/FindIterable.html#projection-org.bson.conversions.Bson-) method to the `find` method. The example uses the [com.mongodb.client.model.Projections](http://mongodb.github.io/mongo-java-driver/3.4/javadoc/com/mongodb/client/model/Projections.html) class to create the projection documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/project-fields-from-query-results.md#return-the-specified-fields-and-the-id-field-only · keywords: projection, find
- [passage] To find documents where `status` is either `new` or `processing`, use [`$in`:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#mongodb-query-op.-in) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#examples · keywords: $in, status, new, processing
- [passage] To perform a case-insensitive regex pattern matching, use the [`i` Option](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexmatch.md#std-label-regexMatch-example-i-options) instead. See [`i` Option](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexmatch.md#std-label-regexMatch-example-i-options) for an example. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexMatch.md#regexmatch-and-collation · keywords: query operator anti-pattern · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexFindAll.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexFind.md
- [passage] Use the `$not` operator with another operator expression. To use `$not` for an inequality check, use: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/not.md#syntax · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $not · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/not/
- [passage] To specify an [`$exists`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#mongodb-query-op.-exists) expression, use the following prototype: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#syntax · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $exists
- [passage] Use the [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) operator to pass either a string containing a JavaScript expression or a full JavaScript function to the query system. The [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) provides greater flexibility, but requires that the database processes the JavaScript expression or function for *each* document in the collection. Reference the document in the JavaScript expression or function using either `this` or `obj` . — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#definition · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $where, this, obj
- [passage] To filter results using a variable in a pipeline [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match) stage, you must access the variable within the [`$expr`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#mongodb-query-op.-expr) operator. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md#use-variables-in-let · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $match, $expr · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md
- [passage] To query for fields that **exist** and are **not null**, use the `{ $ne : null }` filter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#non-equality-filter · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, { $ne : null }
- [passage] To use `$regex` with [`mongodump`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongodump), enclose the query document in single quotes ('\{ ... }') to ensure it doesn't interact with the shell. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#syntax · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $regex, mongodump
- [passage] To include a regular expression in a comma-separated list of query conditions for the field, use the `$regex` operator. For example: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#implicit-and-conditions-for-the-field · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $regex
- [passage] To use either the `x` option or `s` options, you must use the `$regex` operator expression *with* the [`$options`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#mongodb-query-op.-options) operator. For example, to specify the `i` and the `s` options, you must use [`$options`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#mongodb-query-op.-options) for both: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#x-and-s-options · keywords: query operator anti-pattern,  option or ,  options, you must use the ,  operator expression *with* the [,  and the ,  options, you must use [
- [passage] To use PCRE (Perl Compatible Regular Expressions)-supported features in a regular expression that aren't supported in JavaScript, use the `$regex` operator and specify the pattern as a string. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#pcre-versus-javascript · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $regex

## Measurements and reference values

- [fact] The pseudo-random cursor walks the B-tree and is not guaranteed uniform; skew is likelier with unbalanced trees, many deleted documents, or many documents invisible to the transaction. For a uniform sample put another stage (such as $match) before $sample or use N above 5%, accepting the scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample/ · keywords: count, cursor, query operator anti-pattern, Count and Distinct and Sampling Optimization
- [statement] A community benchmark (July 2022) measured $or rising from 52 ms at 1,000 items to 11,684 ms at 20,000, while $in rose from 45 ms to 236 ms; the $or test had no index, so the comparison is unequal and is only directional evidence that $in scales better. — https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/performance-of-or-vs-in/175513 · keywords: $in, index, query operator anti-pattern, $in and $or Index Bounds and Union Plans
- [statement] A low-selectivity $nin on an indexed array field can be slower with the index than without it. In one forum report, the indexed plan examined about 3 million index keys and took about 1,962 ms; the COLLSCAN took about 107 ms. A document matches $nin only if none of its array keys match. The reporter forced a collection scan with hint({$natural:1}). Single anecdote, not a benchmark. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/index-is-slower-when-using-nin/112757 · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [passage] | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `version` | A number that indicates the query engine used to complete the query. `1` indicates that the classic engine was used.; `2` indicates that the [slot-based query execution engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md#std-label-sbe-landing) was used. | | `createdFromQuery` | A document that contains the specific query that resulted in this cache entry. For example: `{ "query" : <document>, "sort" : <document>, "projection" : <document> }` | | `isActive` | A boolean that indicates whether the entry is active or inactive. If active, the query planner is currently using the entry to generate query plans.; If inactive, the query planner is not currently using the entry to generate query plans. See [Plan Cache Entry State.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-state) | | `planCacheShapeHash` | A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of the [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape). See [`explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash) Starting in MongoDB 8.0, the existing `queryHash` field is duplicated in a new field named `planCacheShapeHash`. If you're using an earlier MongoDB version, you'll only see the `queryHash` field. Future MongoDB versions will remove the deprecated `queryHash` field, and you'll need to use the `planCacheShapeHash` field instead. | | `planCacheKey` | A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of the key used to find the plan cache entry associated with this query. The plan cache key is a function of both the [plan cache query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) and the currently available indexes for that shape. See [`explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey) | | `cachedPlan` | The details of the cached plan. The fields included in the `cachedPlan` vary based on whether the query was completed using the classic engine or the slot-based query execution engine. For more information on query plans, see [`explain.queryPlanner`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner) | | `works` | The number of "work units" performed by the query execution plan during the trial period when the query planner evaluates candidate plans. For more information, see [`explain.executionStats.executionStages.works`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.executionStages.works) | | `timeOfCreation` | Time of creation for the entry. | | `creationExecStats` | An array of execution stats documents. The array contains a document for each candidate plan. For details on the execution stats, see [`explain.executionStats`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats) | | `candidatePlanScores` | An array of scores for the candidate plans listed in the `creationExecStats` array. | | `indexFilterSet` | A boolean that indicates whether an [index filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) exists for the [plan cache query shape.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) | | `estimatedSizeBytes` | The estimated size in bytes of a plan cache entry. | | `querySettings` | **New in version 8.0** A document that contains query settings previously set using [`setQuerySettings`:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) `querySettings: { indexHints: [ { ns: { db: <string>, coll: <string> }, allowedIndexes: <array> }, ... ], queryFramework: <string> }` `querySettings` fields: `indexHints.ns` (document): Namespace for index hints.`db` (string): Name of the database for index hints.; `coll` (string): Name of the collection for index hints.; `indexHints.allowedIndexes` (array): Array of indexes for index hints. For more details, see [Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#std-label-indexes) and [`hint()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint); `queryFramework` (string): [Query framework](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-framework) string can be:`classic` for the classic engine.; `sbe` for slot-based query execution engine. For details, see [Slot-Based Query Execution Engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md#std-label-sbe-landing) | | `host` | The hostname and port of the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) instance from which the plan cache information was returned. When run on a sharded cluster, the operation returns plan cache entry information from a single member in each shard replica set. This member is identified with the [shard](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-plancachestats-shard) and [host](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-plancachestats-host) fields. See also [Redaction.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-plancachestats-read-pref) | | `shard` | The name of the shard from which [`$planCacheStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-planCacheStats) retrieved the cache entry. Only available if run on a sharded cluster. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#classic-execution-engine · keywords: cursor, index, projection, query shape, version,  indicates that the classic engine was used.; 
- [passage] - [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) evaluates JavaScript and cannot take advantage of indexes. Therefore, query performance improves when you express your query using the standard MongoDB operators (e.g., [`$gt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gt.md#mongodb-query-op.-gt), [`$in`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#mongodb-query-op.-in)). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#considerations · keywords: $in, index, query operator anti-pattern, query optimization, $where, $gt
- [statement] distinct on a dotted field cannot be covered (SERVER-2104), and SERVER-23582 (closed 2016-05-17) reported the planner choosing a non-multikey DISTINCT_SCAN with a FETCH that cost more than a collection scan; check explain on dotted-field distincts. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-23582 · keywords: count, index, query operator anti-pattern, Count and Distinct and Sampling Optimization
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `key` | document | Specifies the index's fields. For each field, specify a key-value pair in which the key is the name of the field to index and the value is either the index direction or [index type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types.md#std-label-index-types). If specifying direction, specify `1` for ascending or `-1` for descending. MongoDB supports several different index types, including: [text](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-feature-text); [geospatial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/geospatial-queries.md#std-label-index-feature-geospatial); [hashed indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed.md#std-label-index-type-hashed) See [index types](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types.md#std-label-index-types) for more information. [Wildcard indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard.md#std-label-wildcard-index-core) support workloads where users query against custom fields or a large variety of fields in a collection: You can create a wildcard index on a specific field and its subpaths or on all of the fields in a document.For details see, [Wildcard Indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard.md#std-label-wildcard-index-core) | | `name` | string | A name that uniquely identifies the index. | | `unique` | boolean | Optional. Creates a unique index so that the collection will not accept insertion or update of documents where the index key value matches an existing value in the index. Specify `true` to create a unique index. The default value is `false`. The option is *unavailable* for [hashed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed.md#std-label-index-hashed-index) indexes. | | `partialFilterExpression` | document | Optional. If specified, the index only references documents that match the filter expression. See [Partial Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md) for more information. A filter expression can include: equality expressions (i.e. `field: value` or using the [`$eq`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#mongodb-query-op.-eq) operator); [`$exists: true`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#mongodb-query-op.-exists) expression; [`$gt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gt.md#mongodb-query-op.-gt), [`$gte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gte.md#mongodb-query-op.-gte), [`$lt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lt.md#mongodb-query-op.-lt), [`$lte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lte.md#mongodb-query-op.-lte) expressions; [`$type`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/type.md#mongodb-query-op.-type) expressions; [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator; [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) operator; [`$in`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#mongodb-query-op.-in) operator; [`$geoWithin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geowithin.md#mongodb-query-op.-geoWithin) operator; [`$geoIntersects`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geointersects.md#mongodb-query-op.-geoIntersects) operator If you are using [Client-Side Field Level Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/csfle.md#std-label-manual-csfle-feature) or [Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption.md#std-label-qe-manual-feature-qe), a `partialFilterExpression` cannot reference an encrypted field. You can specify a `partialFilterExpression` option for all MongoDB [index types.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types.md#std-label-index-types) | | `sparse` | boolean | Optional. If `true`, the index only references documents with the specified field. These indexes use less space but behave differently in some situations (particularly sorts). The default value is `false`. See [Sparse Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md) for more information. The following index types are sparse by default and ignore this option: [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index); [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index); [Text](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-type-text) For a compound index that includes `2dsphere` index key(s) along with keys of other types, only the `2dsphere` index fields determine whether the index references a document. MongoDB provides the option to create [partial indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial). These offer a superset of the functionality of sparse indexes and are preferred instead. | | `expireAfterSeconds` | integer | Optional. Specifies a value, in seconds, as a time to live ([TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-TTL)) to control how long MongoDB retains documents in this collection. This option only applies to [TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-TTL) indexes. See [Expire Data from Collections by Setting TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/expire-data.md#std-label-ttl-collections) for more information. If you use TTL indexes created before MongoDB 5.0, or if you want to sync data created in MongDB 5.0 with a pre-5.0 installation, see [Indexes Configured Using NaN](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/expire-data.md#std-label-expireData-warning) to avoid misconfiguration issues. The TTL index `expireAfterSeconds` value must be within `0` and `2147483647` inclusive. | | [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#std-label-cmd-createIndexes-hidden) | boolean | Optional. A hidden index is not evaluated as part of query plan selection. Default is `false`. | | `storageEngine` | document | Optional. You can specify weights for some or all the indexed fields. The default value is `1`. | | `default_language` | string | Optional. This option is only valid if creating a [wildcard index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard.md#std-label-wildcard-index-core) on all document fields. You cannot specify this option if creating a wildcard index on a specific field path and its subfields, e.g. `{ "path.to.field.$**" : 1 }` The `wildcardProjection` option takes the following form: `wildcardProjection: { "path.to.field.a" : <value>, "path.to.field.b" : <value> }` The `<value>` can be either of the following: `1` or `true` to include the field in the wildcard index.; `0` or `false` to exclude the field from the wildcard index. Wildcard indexes omit the `_id` field by default. To include the `_id` field in the wildcard index, you must explicitly include it in the `wildcardProjection` document: `{ "wildcardProjection": { "_id": 1, "<field>": 0|1 } }` All of the statements in the `wildcardProjection` document must be either inclusion or exclusion statements. You can also include the `_id` field with exclusion statements. WARNING: Avoid performing rolling index and replicated index build processes concurrently as it might lead to unexpected issues, such as broken builds and crash loops. You can only build rolling indexes on M10+ Clusters. During a rolling index build, Atlas takes each node out of the replica set, starts it in standalone mode to build the index, and then returns it to the replica set. This process repeats for each node in the cluster in a rolling sequence. Nodes may appear as down, while Atlas builds indexes offline. This is expected behavior, not an issue. | [Rolling Index Builds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/rolling-index-builds.md#std-label-rolling-index-build) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/indexes.md#create-an-index · keywords: index, projection, query operator anti-pattern, unique, timezone, { "timezone": { "$exists": true } }

- [passage] However, the following query cannot use the partial index on the `name` field because using the index results in an incomplete result set. Specifically, the query predicate includes the condition `password: { $exists: false }` while the index has the filter `password: { $exists: true }`. That is, the query `{ name: "Ned Stark", password: { $exists: false } }` matches more documents (users without passwords) than the index covers. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#query-coverage · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, query shape, name, password: { $exists: false }, password: { $exists: true }
- [passage] [Multikey indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#std-label-index-type-multikey) cannot cover queries over array fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#multikey-covering · keywords: index, projection
- [statement] Very large $or lists were slow in the planner because IndexBoundsBuilder::unionize() merged clause bounds one at a time (roughly quadratic); SERVER-34012 was fixed in 5.0.0-rc0. The reporter's diagnostic patch cut a 20,000-clause query from ~40 s to ~400 ms; the official fix's gain is not stated. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-34012 · keywords: $in, index, $in and $or Index Bounds and Union Plans
- [fact] Not every index type can cover queries; hashed indexes cannot be multikey, and support must be checked on each index type's docs page. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, projection, Projection Optimization and Covered Query Design
- [fact] Even when a query cannot be covered, projecting only needed fields reduces network traffic and processing time; coverage additionally removes document reads, so a covered design should index filter fields first (ESR order) and then projected-only fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, projection, Projection Optimization and Covered Query Design
- [passage] You *cannot* use `$regex` operator expressions inside an [`$in`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#mongodb-query-op.-in) operator. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#in-expressions · keywords: $in, query operator anti-pattern, $regex
- [passage] db.movies.find( { rated: { $exists: true } }, { _id: 0, title: 1, rated: 1 } ).limit( 3 ) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists/ · keywords: projection, query operator anti-pattern
- [passage] db.movies.find( { rated: { $exists: false } }, { _id: 0, title: 1, year: 1 } ).limit( 3 ) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists/ · keywords: projection, query operator anti-pattern
- [passage] For example, a comparison between `$a` and a constant value can use an index, but a comparison between `$a` and `$b` cannot. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#expr-in-lookup-operations · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, $a, $b
- [fact] Case-insensitive indexes (collation) do not help $regex, because $regex is not collation-aware. The case-insensitive (i) option therefore forfeits efficient prefix bounds. The wording 'cannot use any index' is stronger than the docs; the safer reading is 'no efficient bounds', and explain() decides. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/reference/operator/query/regex/ · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)
- [fact] $where evaluates JavaScript for each document and cannot take advantage of indexes. Alone it requires a collection scan. MongoDB evaluates the non-$where predicates first, and those can use an index, so always pair $where with at least one indexable standard predicate. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)
- [fact] $exists:false cannot use a sparse index (requires a COLLSCAN) and requires a FETCH on a non-sparse index. $exists:true is most efficient on a sparse index (exact match, no FETCH). To exclude null and missing values, {field:{$ne:null}} avoids needing a sparse index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists/ · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)
- [passage] When a query specifies an exact match for an array as a whole, MongoDB uses the multikey index to locate documents that contain the first element of that array. However, it cannot match the entire array using the index alone. MongoDB then fetches the candidate documents and filters them to return only those whose array exactly matches the query array. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: index, projection · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md
- [passage] | Rule | Valid Example | Invalid Example | | --- | --- | --- | | If you specify a `wildcardProjection`, it cannot be empty. | `{ productId: 1, "$**": 1 }, { wildcardProjection: { attributes: 1 } }` | `{ productId: 1, "$**": 1 }, { wildcardProjection: { } }` | | You can only combine inclusions and exclusions in a `wildcardProjection` if the included or excluded field is `_id`. - [fact] Multikey indexes can cover queries over non-array fields (the index tracks which fields make it multikey) but cannot cover queries over array fields. A multikey index covers a query only if the projection does not return the array field and the query does not use $elemMatch; to cover a query that filters on the array field, the index must be compound. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, projection, Projection Optimization and Covered Query Design
- [fact] To confirm coverage, read explain("executionStats"): look for IXSCAN directly under PROJECTION_COVERED with no FETCH and totalDocsExamined: 0. Flexible schema means MongoDB cannot assume indexed fields exist in all documents, so any projection not fully satisfied by index keys keeps FETCH. — https://dev.to/franckpachot/index-only-scan-on-json-documents-with-covering-and-multi-key-indexes-in-mongodb-53h4 · keywords: index, projection, Projection Optimization and Covered Query Design

- [passage] | Operand | Description | | --- | --- | | `<array expression>` | Any valid [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) if it resolves to an array. | | `<position>` | Optional. Any valid [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) if it resolves to an integer. If positive, [`$slice`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/slice.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-slice) determines the starting position from the start of the array. If `<position>` is greater than the number of elements, the [`$slice`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/slice.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-slice) returns an empty array.; If negative, [`$slice`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/slice.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-slice) determines the starting position from the end of the array. If the absolute value of the `<position>` is greater than the number of elements, the starting position is the start of the array. | | `<n>` | Any valid [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) as long as it resolves to an integer. If `<position>` is specified, `<n>` must resolve to a positive integer. If positive, [`$slice`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/slice.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-slice) returns up to the first `n` elements in the array. If the `<position>` is specified, [`$slice`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/slice.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-slice) returns the first `n` elements starting from the position.; If negative, [`$slice`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/slice.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-slice) returns up to the last `n` elements in the array. `n` cannot resolve to a negative number *if* `<position>` is specified. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/slice.md#definition · keywords: projection, <array expression>, <position>, $slice, <n>,  elements in the array. - [passage] | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `from` | Target collection for the [`$graphLookup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/graphlookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-graphLookup) operation to search, recursively matching the `connectFromField` to the `connectToField`. The `from` collection must be in the same database as any other collections used in the operation. For sharding support, see [Sharded Collections.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/graphlookup.md#std-label-graphLookup-sharded-collections) | | `startWith` | [Expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) that specifies the value of the `connectFromField` with which to start the recursive search. If `startWith` evaluates to an array, `$graphLookup` performs the search simultaneously from all array elements. | | `connectFromField` | Field name whose value [`$graphLookup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/graphlookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-graphLookup) uses to recursively match against the `connectToField` of other documents in the collection. If the value is an array, each element is individually followed through the traversal process. | | `connectToField` | Field name in other documents against which to match the value of the field specified by the `connectFromField` parameter. | | `as` | Name of the array field added to each output document. Contains the documents traversed in the [`$graphLookup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/graphlookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-graphLookup) stage to reach the document. Documents returned in the `as` field are not guaranteed to be in any order. | | `maxDepth` | *Optional.* Non-negative integral number specifying the maximum recursion depth. | | `depthField` | *Optional.* Name of the field to add to each traversed document in the search path. The value of this field is the recursion depth for the document, represented as a [`NumberLong`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mongodb-extended-json-v1.md#mongodb-bsontype-data_numberlong). Recursion depth value starts at zero, so the first lookup corresponds to zero depth. | | `restrictSearchWithMatch` | *Optional.* A document specifying additional conditions for the recursive search. The syntax is identical to [query filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents.md#std-label-read-operations-query-argument) syntax. You cannot use any [aggregation expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) in this filter. For example, you can't use the following document to find documents in which the `lastName` value is different from the `lastName` value of the input document: `{ lastName: { $ne: "$lastName" } }` You can't use the document in this context, because `"$lastName"` will act as a string literal, not a field path. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/graphLookup.md#definition · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, from, $graphLookup, connectFromField, connectToField, startWith
- [passage] | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | [input](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexmatch.md#std-label-regexMatch-input) | The string on which you wish to apply the [regex pattern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexmatch.md#std-label-regexMatch-regex). Can be a string or any valid [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) that resolves to a string. | | [regex](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexmatch.md#std-label-regexMatch-regex) | The regex pattern to apply. Can be any valid [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) that resolves to either a string or regex pattern `/<pattern>/`. When using the regex `/<pattern>/`, you can also specify the regex options `i` and `m` (but not the `s` or `x` options): `"pattern"`; `/<pattern>/`; `/<pattern>/<options>` Alternatively, you can also specify the regex options with the [options](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexmatch.md#std-label-regexMatch-options) field. To specify the `s` or `x` options, you must use the [options](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexmatch.md#std-label-regexMatch-options) field. You cannot specify options in both the `regex` and the `options` field. | | [options](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexmatch.md#std-label-regexMatch-options) | *Optional*. The following `<options>` are available for use with regular expression. You cannot specify options in both the `regex` and the `options` field. `i`: Case insensitivity to match both upper and lower cases. You can specify the option in the `options` field or as part of the regex field.; `m`: For patterns that include anchors (that is, `^` for the start, `$` for the end), match at the beginning or end of each line for strings with multiline values. Without this option, these anchors match at beginning or end of the string.If the pattern contains no anchors or if the string value has no newline characters (e.g. `\n`), the `m` option has no effect.; `x`: "Extended" capability to ignore all white space characters in the pattern unless escaped or included in a character class.Additionally, it ignores characters in-between and including an un-escaped hash/pound (`#`) character and the next new line, so that you may include comments in complicated patterns. This only applies to data characters; white space characters may never appear within special character sequences in a pattern.The `x` option does not affect the handling of the VT character (code 11).You can specify the option only in the `options` field.; `s`: Allows the dot character (`.`) to match all characters *including* newline characters.You can specify the option only in the `options` field. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexMatch.md#syntax · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, /<pattern>/,  and ,  (but not the ,  or ,  options):  · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexFindAll.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/regexFind.md
- [passage] - The `$text` operator expression cannot appear in [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/or.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-or) or [`$not`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/not.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-not) expressions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#restrictions · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $text, $or, $not
- [passage] | Keyword | Type | Definition | Behavior | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | additionalItems | arrays | boolean or object | If an object, must be a valid JSON Schema | | additionalProperties | objects | boolean or object | If `true`, additional fields are allowed. If `false`, they are not. If a valid JSON Schema object is specified, additional fields must validate against the schema. Starting in MongoDB 5.1, if the `description` field is specified, MongoDB includes the `description` in the error output when a document fails validation. | | enum | all types | array of values | Enumerates all possible values of the field | | exclusiveMaximum | numbers | boolean | If true and field is a number, `maximum` is an exclusive maximum. Available types are "object", "array", "number", "boolean", "string", and "null". MongoDB's implementation of the JSON Schema does not support the "integer" type. Use the `bsonType` keyword and the "int" or "long" types instead. | | uniqueItems | arrays | boolean | If true, each item in the array must be unique. Otherwise, no uniqueness constraint is enforced. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/jsonSchema.md#available-keywords · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, true, false, $type, description, maximum
- [passage] - You cannot use [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) in a `$match` stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#restrictions · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $where, $match
- [passage] [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) no longer supports the deprecated [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) JavaScript code with scope (BSON Type 15). The [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) operator only supports BSON type String (BSON Type 2) or BSON type JavaScript (BSON Type 13). The use of BSON type JavaScript with scope for [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) has been deprecated since MongoDB 4.2.1. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#syntax · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $where
- [passage] [`map-reduce operations`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/mapreduce.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.mapReduce) and [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) operator expressions **cannot** access certain global functions or properties, such as `db`, that are available in [`mongosh`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#available-javascript-properties-and-functions · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, map-reduce operations, $where, db, mongosh
- [passage] To find documents that contain BSON regular expressions as values, call `find()` with the `bsonRegExp` option set to `true`. The `bsonRegExp` option allows you to return regular expressions that can't be represented as JavaScript regular expressions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#query-for-bson-regular-expressions · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, find(), bsonRegExp, true
- [passage] Queries that compare an encrypted field to `null` or a regular expression always throw an error, even if using a supported query operator. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/reference/supported-operations.md#unsupported-queries · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, null
