## Comparisons and alternatives

- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `planCacheSetFilter` | string | The name of the collection for the index filter. | | `query` | document | The query predicate for the index filter. Only the predicate structure, including the field names, is used in the index filter. The field values in the query predicate are not used. Therefore, the query predicate in an index filter is used by similar queries that differ only in the field values. | | `sort` | document | Optional. The sort for the index filter. | | `projection` | document | Optional. The projection for the index filter. | | `collation` | document | Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. Starting in MongoDB 6.0, an index filter uses the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) previously set using the [`planCacheSetFilter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/plancachesetfilter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.planCacheSetFilter) command. Starting in MongoDB 8.0, use query settings instead of adding [index filters](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters). Index filters are deprecated starting in MongoDB 8.0. Query settings have more functionality than index filters. Also, index filters aren't persistent and you cannot easily create index filters for all cluster nodes. To add query settings and explore examples, see [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) | | `indexes` | array | An array of index filters for the specified plan cache query shape. Specify the index filters as one of these arrays: Index specification documents. For example, `[ { x : 1 }, ... ]`.; Index names. For example, `[ "x_1", ... ]`. The [query optimizer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization) uses either a collection scan or the index arrays for the query plan. If the specified indexes do not exist or are [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md), the optimizer uses a collection scan. For multiple indexes with the same key pattern, you must specify the index as an array of names. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#command-fields · keywords: cursor, index, projection, query optimization, query shape, planCacheSetFilter · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClearFilters.md
- [passage] | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `filter` | document | The selection criteria for the update. The same [query selectors](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/query-predicates.md#std-label-query-selectors) as in the [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) method are available. To update the first document returned in the collection, specify an empty document `{ }`. If unspecified, defaults to an empty document. If the query field is not a document, the operation returns an error. If no document matches the `filter`, no document is updated. | | `update` | document or array | The update document or an [aggregation pipeline.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline.md#std-label-aggregation-pipeline) If passed a document with [update operator expressions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/update.md#std-label-update-operators), `findOneAndUpdate()` performs the specified modification.The document must contain only [update operators](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/update.md#std-label-update-operators-top-level). You cannot specify a replacement document `{ <field1>: <value1>, ...}`. To use a replacement document, see [`db.collection.findOneAndReplace()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findoneandreplace.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.findOneAndReplace) instead.; If passed an [aggregation pipeline](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline.md#std-label-aggregation-pipeline) `[ <stage1>, <stage2>, ... ]`, `findOneAndUpdate()` modifies the document per the pipeline. The pipeline can consist of the following stages:[`$addFields`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/addfields.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-addFields) and its alias [`$set`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/set.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-set); [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) and its alias [`$unset`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unset.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-unset); [`$replaceRoot`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/replaceroot.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-replaceRoot) and its alias [`$replaceWith`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/replacewith.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-replaceWith) | | `writeConcern` | document | Optional. A document expressing the [write concern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern.md#std-label-write-concern). Omit to use the default write concern. `{ w: <value>, j: <boolean>, wtimeout: <number> }` Do not explicitly set the write concern for the operation if run in a transaction. To use write concern with transactions, see [Transactions and Write Concern.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md#std-label-transactions-write-concern) | | `projection` | document | Optional. A subset of fields to return. To return all fields in the returned document, omit this parameter. If the projection argument is not a document, the operation errors. | | `sort` | document | Optional. Specifies a sorting order for the documents matched by the `filter`. If the sort argument is not a document, the operation errors. See [`cursor.sort()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) | | `maxTimeMS` | number | Optional. Specifies a time limit in milliseconds within which the operation must complete within. Throws an error if the limit is exceeded. | | `upsert` | boolean | Optional. When `true`, [`findOneAndUpdate()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findoneandupdate.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.findOneAndUpdate) either: Creates a new document if no documents match the `filter`. For more details see [upsert behavior](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.update.md#std-label-upsert-behavior). Returns `null` after inserting the new document, unless `returnNewDocument` is `true`.; Updates a single document that matches the `filter`. To avoid multiple [upserts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-upsert), ensure that the `filter` field(s) are [uniquely indexed.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#std-label-index-type-unique) Defaults to `false`, which does *not* insert a new document when no match is found. | | `returnDocument` | string | Optional. Starting in [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) 0.13.2, `returnDocument` is an alternative for `returnNewDocument`. If both options are set, `returnDocument` takes precedence. `returnDocument: "before"` returns the original document. `returnDocument: "after"` returns the updated document. | | `returnNewDocument` | boolean | Optional. When `true`, returns the updated document instead of the original document. Defaults to `false`. | | `collation` | document | Optional. Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. | | `arrayFilters` | array | Optional. An array of filter documents that determine which array elements to modify for an update operation on an array field. In the update document, use the [`$[<identifier>]`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/update/positional-filtered.md#mongodb-update-up.---identifier--) filtered positional operator to define an identifier, which you then reference in the array filter documents. You cannot have an array filter document for an identifier if the identifier is not included in the update document. The `<identifier>` must begin with a lowercase letter and contain only alphanumeric characters. You can include the same identifier multiple times in the update document; however, for each distinct identifier (`$[identifier]`) in the update document, you must specify **exactly one** corresponding array filter document. That is, you cannot specify multiple array filter documents for the same identifier. For example, if the update statement includes the identifier `x` (possibly multiple times), you cannot specify the following for `arrayFilters` that includes 2 separate filter documents for `x`: `// INVALID — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findOneAndUpdate.md#parameters · keywords: cursor, index, projection, query shape, filter, find() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findOneAndReplace.md
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `query` | document | Optional. The selection criteria for the modification. The `query` field employs the same [query selectors](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/query-predicates.md#std-label-query-selectors) as used in the [`db.collection.find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) method. Although the query may match multiple documents, [`findAndModify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.findAndModify) **selects only one document to update**. If unspecified, defaults to an empty document. If the query argument is not a document, the operation errors. | | `sort` | document | Optional. Determines which document the operation updates if the query selects multiple documents. [`findAndModify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.findAndModify) updates the first document in the sort order specified by this argument. If the sort argument is not a document, the operation errors. MongoDB does not store documents in a collection in a particular order. When sorting on a field which contains duplicate values, documents containing those values may be returned in any order. The `$sort` operation is not a "stable sort," which means that documents with equivalent sort keys are not guaranteed to remain in the same relative order in the output as they were in the input. If the field specified in the sort criteria does not exist in two documents, then the value on which they are sorted is the same. The two documents may be returned in any order. If consistent sort order is desired, include at least one field in your sort that contains unique values. The easiest way to guarantee this is to include the `_id` field in your sort query. See [Sort Consistency](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#std-label-sort-cursor-consistent-sorting) for more information. | | `remove` | boolean | Must specify either the `remove` or the `update` field. Removes the document specified in the `query` field. Set this to `true` to remove the selected document . The default is `false`. | | `update` | document or array | Must specify either the `remove` or the `update` field. Performs an update of the selected document. If passed a document with [update operator expressions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/update.md#std-label-update-operators), [`findAndModify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.findAndModify) performs the specified modification.; If passed a replacement document `{ <field1>: <value1>, ...}`, the [`findAndModify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.findAndModify) performs a replacement.; If passed an [aggregation pipeline](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline.md#std-label-aggregation-pipeline) `[ <stage1>, <stage2>, ... ]`, [`findAndModify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.findAndModify) updates the document per the pipeline. The pipeline can consist of the following stages:[`$addFields`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/addfields.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-addFields) and its alias [`$set`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/set.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-set); [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) and its alias [`$unset`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unset.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-unset); [`$replaceRoot`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/replaceroot.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-replaceRoot) and its alias [`$replaceWith`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/replacewith.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-replaceWith) | | `new` | boolean | Optional. When `true`, returns the updated document rather than the original. The default is `false`. | | `fields` | document | Optional. A subset of fields to return. The `fields` document specifies an inclusion of a field with `1`, as in: `fields: { <field1>: 1, <field2>: 1, ... }`. See [Projection.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#std-label-find-projection) If the fields argument is not a document, the operation errors. | | `upsert` | boolean | Optional. Used in conjunction with the `update` field. When `true`, [`findAndModify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.findAndModify) either: Creates a new document if no documents match the `query`. For more details see [upsert behavior.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.update.md#std-label-upsert-behavior); Updates a single document that matches the `query`. To avoid multiple [upserts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-upsert), ensure that the `query` field(s) are [uniquely indexed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#std-label-index-type-unique). See [Upsert with Unique Index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#std-label-upsert-and-unique-index-dbcommand) for an example. Defaults to `false`, which does *not* insert a new document when no match is found. | | `bypassDocumentValidation` | boolean | Optional. Enables [`findAndModify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.findAndModify) to bypass schema validation during the operation. This lets you update documents that do not meet the validation requirements. | | `writeConcern` | document | Optional. Specifies the [write concern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern.md#std-label-write-concern). Omit to use the default write concern. Do not explicitly set the write concern for the operation if run in a transaction. To use write concern with transactions, see [Transactions and Write Concern.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md#std-label-transactions-write-concern) | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional. Specifies a time limit in milliseconds. If you do not specify a value for `maxTimeMS`, operations will not time out. A value of `0` explicitly specifies the default unbounded behavior. MongoDB terminates operations that exceed their allotted time limit using the same mechanism as [`db.killOp()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killop.md#mongodb-method-db.killOp). MongoDB only terminates an operation at one of its designated [interrupt points.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-interrupt-point) | | `findAndModify` | string | The collection against which to run the command. | | `collation` | document | Optional. Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. | | `arrayFilters` | array | Optional. An array of filter documents that determine which array elements to modify for an update operation on an array field. In the update document, use the [`$[<identifier>]`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/update/positional-filtered.md#mongodb-update-up.---identifier--) filtered positional operator to define an identifier, which you then reference in the array filter documents. You cannot have an array filter document for an identifier if the identifier is not included in the update document. The `<identifier>` must begin with a lowercase letter and contain only alphanumeric characters. You can include the same identifier multiple times in the update document; however, for each distinct identifier (`$[identifier]`) in the update document, you must specify **exactly one** corresponding array filter document. That is, you cannot specify multiple array filter documents for the same identifier. For example, if the update statement includes the identifier `x` (possibly multiple times), you cannot specify the following for `arrayFilters` that includes 2 separate filter documents for `x`: `// INVALID — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findAndModify.md#command-fields · keywords: cursor, index, projection, query shape, query, db.collection.find() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findAndModify.md
- [fact] Adding an array field to a compound index to 'complete' coverage can backfire: in a forum case the index became multikey, the plan fell back to PROJECTION_SIMPLE (not covered), and the poster measured 100 s vs 6 s versus the index without the array field (5.1M docs, MongoDB 4.0.10). — https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/adding-the-projected-fields-to-compound-index-to-create-covered-query-doesnt-improve-performance/199267 · keywords: index, projection, query operator anti-pattern, Projection Optimization and Covered Query Design
- [passage] | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `unique` | boolean | Optional. Specifies that each index specified in the `keyPatterns` array is a [unique index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#std-label-index-type-unique). Unique indexes will not accept insertion or update of documents where the index key value matches an existing value in the index. Specify `true` to create a unique index. The default value is `false`. The option is *unavailable* for [hashed indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed.md#std-label-index-hashed-index) | | `name` | string | Optional. The name of the index. If unspecified, MongoDB generates an index name by concatenating the names of the indexed fields and the sort order. Options specified to [`db.collection.createIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes) apply to **all** of the index specifications included in the key pattern array. Since index names must be unique, you may only specify name if you are creating a single index using [`db.collection.createIndexes()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes) | | `partialFilterExpression` | document | Optional. If `true`, the indexes only reference documents with the specified fields. These indexes use less space but behave differently in some situations (particularly sorts). The default value is `false`. See [Sparse Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) for more information. The following index types are sparse by default and ignore this option: [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index); [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index); [Text](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-type-text) For a compound index that includes `2dsphere` index keys and keys for other types, only the `2dsphere` index fields determine whether the index references a document. [Partial indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) have a superset of the sparse index functionality. Unless your application has a specific requirement, use partial indexes instead of sparse indexes. | | `expireAfterSeconds` | integer | Optional. - [statement] Rewrite negation as a positive predicate where the allowed set is small or known: use $in over the wanted values instead of $nin over excluded values, and add an indexable equality or range predicate so the negation only filters a small residue. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/index-is-slower-when-using-nin/112757 · keywords: $in, query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)
- [fact] An index covers a query only if all query fields (including those needed internally, e.g. for sharding) and all returned fields are in the same index, and no query field is compared to null ({field: null} or {field: {$eq: null}} cannot be covered). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, projection, Projection Optimization and Covered Query Design

- [passage] - Can use `$ne: null` instead of `$exists: true`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#use-a-sparse-index-to-improve-exists-performance · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, $ne: null, $exists: true · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists/
- [fact] Unanchored $regex (no literal ^ prefix, e.g. /^.*laptop/ or /laptop/) cannot build a range. With an index it may still run a full IXSCAN over every key rather than a COLLSCAN; without an index it scans the collection. Either way cost grows with collection size. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/reference/operator/query/regex/ · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)
- [statement] Documented $expr index limits (in the $lookup subpipeline section): only $eq, $lt, $lte, $gt and $gte can use an index, and only for field-vs-constant comparisons. $a vs $b cannot use an index. Multikey, partial and sparse indexes are not used there. The page documents this only for $lookup; the general find() case is not stated in the fetched text. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)
- [fact] $ne, $nin and $not match documents that lack the field. {$not:{$gt:180}} differs from {$lte:180}, which returns only documents where the field exists. Negation therefore returns a large share of the collection and is poorly selective. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/not/ · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)
- [passage] Although you can express this query using the [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) operator, use the [`$in`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#mongodb-query-op.-in) operator rather than the [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) operator when performing equality checks on the same field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/crud/read.md#specify-conditions-using-query-operators · keywords: $in, $or · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md
- [passage] The argument to [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemmatch.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-elemMatch) matches elements of the array that `$elemMatch` is projecting. If you specify an equality with a field name to `$elemMatch`, it attempts to match objects within the array. - [statement] Older servers label covered plans PROJECTION rather than PROJECTION_COVERED (observed on 4.0 vs 5.0.13), so totalDocsExamined: 0 is the version-robust coverage check. — https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/adding-the-projected-fields-to-compound-index-to-create-covered-query-doesnt-improve-performance/199267 · keywords: projection, Projection Optimization and Covered Query Design
- [passage] `{ $not: { $gt: 180 } }` differs from the [`$lte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lte.md#mongodb-query-op.-lte) operator. `{ $lte: 180 }` returns *only* the documents where the `runtime` field exists and its value is less than or equal to `180`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/not.md#syntax · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, { $not: { $gt: 180 } }, $lte, { $lte: 180 }, runtime, 180 · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/not/

## Facts and statements

- [passage] Indexes can also [cover](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#std-label-covered-queries) [`db.collection.distinct()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.distinct.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.distinct) operations. - [passage] The following example creates an index filter on the `orders` collection such that for queries that consist only of an equality match on the `status` field without any projection and sort, the query optimizer evaluates only the two specified indexes and the collection scan for the winning plan: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#set-filter-on-plan-cache-query-shape-consisting-of-predicate-only · keywords: index, projection, query optimization, query shape, orders, status
- [passage] For the plan cache query shape, the query optimizer will only consider indexed plans which use the index `{ item: 1, order_date: 1, quantity: 1 }`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#set-filter-on-plan-cache-query-shape-consisting-of-predicate-projection-and-sort · keywords: index, projection, query optimization, query shape, { item: 1, order_date: 1, quantity: 1 }
- [statement] If maxTimeMS equals the driver's client socket timeout, the driver closes the connection first and the server can never return MaxTimeMSExpired, causing connection churn. Set the client timeout above maxTimeMS. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-2971 · keywords: cursor, query operator anti-pattern, read preference, Cursor and Read-Path Tuning (batchSize and maxTimeMS and read preference)

- [fact] Hashed sharding gives more even distribution at the cost of targeting. - [passage] An aggregation pipeline can use [indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#std-label-indexes) from the input collection to improve performance. Using an index limits the amount of documents a stage processes. Ideally, an index can [cover](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#std-label-read-operations-covered-query) the stage query. A covered query has especially high performance, since the index returns all matching documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#indexes · keywords: index, projection, query optimization

- [fact] For case-sensitive $regex, an index lets MongoDB match the regex against index values, which can beat a collection scan. If the regex is a prefix expression (starts with ^ or \A followed by simple symbols), MongoDB builds an index range from the prefix and scans only that range. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/reference/operator/query/regex/ · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)
- [fact] /^a/, /^a.*/ and /^a.*$/ match equivalent strings and all can use an index, but /^a.*/ and /^a.*$/ are slower. /^a/ can stop scanning after the prefix. Write the bare anchored prefix, not a trailing .*. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/reference/operator/query/regex/ · keywords: index, query operator anti-pattern, Query Operator Anti-Patterns ($regex and negation and $where and $expr and $exists)

- [passage] | Value | Description | | --- | --- | | `$slice: <number>` | Specifies the number of elements to return in the `<arrayField>`. For `<number>`: Specify a positive number `n` to return the first `n` elements.; Specify a negative number `n` to return the last `n` elements. If the `<number>` is greater than the number of array elements, the query returns all array elements. | | `$slice: [ <number to skip>, <number to return> ]` | Specifies the number of elements to return in the `<arrayField>` after skipping the specified number of elements starting from the first element. You must specify both elements. For the `<number to skip>`: Specify a positive number `n` to skip `n` elements from the start of the array; i.e. 0th index position. Based on a zero-based array index, `1` indicates the starting position of the 2nd element, etc. If `n` is greater than the number of array elements, the query returns an empty array for the `<arrayField>`.; Specify a negative number `n` to skip backward `n` elements from the start of the array; i.e. 0th index position Based on a zero-based array index (i.e. the first element is at index 0), `-1` indicates the starting position of the last element, etc. If the absolute value of the negative number is greater than the number of array elements, the starting position is the start of the array. For the `<number to return>`, you must specify a *positive* number `n` to return the next `n` elements, starting after skipping the specified number. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/slice.md#syntax · keywords: index, projection, $slice: <number>, <arrayField>, <number>,  to return the first

- [passage] | Projection | Description | | --- | --- | | `<field>: <1 or true>` | Specifies the inclusion of a field. If you specify a non-zero integer for the projection value, the operation treats the value as `true`. | | `<field>: <0 or false>` | Specifies the exclusion of a field. | | `"<field>.$": <1 or true>` | Uses the [`$`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/positional.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-) array projection operator to return the first element that matches the query condition on the array field. If you specify a non-zero integer for the projection value, the operation treats the value as `true`. Not available for [views.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md#std-label-views-landing-page) | | `<field>: <array projection>` | Uses the array projection operators ([`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemmatch.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-elemMatch), [`$slice`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/slice.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-slice)) to specify the array elements to include. Not available for [views.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md#std-label-views-landing-page) | | `<field>: <aggregation expression>` | Specifies the value of the projected field. With the use of [aggregation expressions and syntax](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions), including the use of literals and aggregation variables, you can project new fields or project existing fields with new values. If you specify a non-numeric, non-boolean literal (such as a literal string or an array or an operator expression) for the projection value, the field is projected with the new value, for example:`{ field: [ 1, 2, 3, "$someExistingField" ] }`; `{ field: "New String Value" }`; `{ field: { status: "Active", total: { $sum: "$existingArray" } } }`; To project a literal value for a field, use the [`$literal`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/literal.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-literal) aggregation expression, for example:`{ field: { $literal: 5 } }`; `{ field: { $literal: true } }`; `{ field: { $literal: { fieldWithValue0: 0, fieldWithValue1: 1 } } }` | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findOneAndUpdate.md#projection · keywords: projection, <field>: <1 or true>, true, <field>: <0 or false>, "<field>.$": <1 or true>, <field>: <array projection> · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findOneAndDelete.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findAndModify.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findOneAndReplace.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md

- [passage] - If the projection of the embedded document comes after any and all projections of its fields, MongoDB projects the embedded document. For example, the projection document `{ "size.uom": 1, size: 1 }` produces the same result as the projection document `{ size: 1 }`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#operations · keywords: projection, { "size.uom": 1, size: 1 }, { size: 1 }
- [passage] - If the projection of the embedded document comes before the projection any of its fields, MongoDB projects the specified field or fields. - [passage] The [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) operator has the following form: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#syntax · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $where
- [passage] - However, if you must create custom expressions, [`$function`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/function.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-function) is preferred over [`$where`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#syntax · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $function, $where · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/function.md
- [passage] The following JavaScript functions and properties **are available** to [`map-reduce operations`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/mapreduce.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.mapReduce) and [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) operator expressions: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#available-javascript-properties-and-functions · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, map-reduce operations, $where
- [passage] Only apply the [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) query operator to top-level documents. The [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) query operator will not work inside a nested document, for instance, in an [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch.md#mongodb-query-op.-elemMatch) query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#elemmatch · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $where, $elemMatch
- [passage] Using normal non-[`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) query statements provides the following performance advantages: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#considerations · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $where
- [passage] The following example uses [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) and the `hex_md5()` JavaScript function to compare the value of the `name` field to an MD5 hash and returns any matching document. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#example · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $where, hex_md5(), name
- [passage] If you must create custom expressions, [`$function`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/function.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-function) is preferred over [`$where`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#example · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $function, $where
- [passage] [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) does not permit references to the `db` object from the [`$where`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md#mongodb-query-op.-where) function. This is uncommon in un-sharded collections. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#sharding-operational-restrictions · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $where, db
- [passage] If a field is missing from a document, [`$ne`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/ne.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-ne) treats the missing field as a distinct value, separate from `null`. [`$ne`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/ne.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-ne) considers two missing fields equivalent to each other, and considers a missing field different from a `null` value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/ne.md#definition · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $ne, null
- [passage] The [`$ne`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/ne.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-ne) compares both value and type, using the [specified BSON comparison order](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-type-comparison-order.md#std-label-bson-types-comparison-order) for values of different types. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/ne.md#definition · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $ne
- [passage] | Field | Description | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | `match` | An ECMAScript-formatted regular expression (regex) to match against a provided username. Each parenthesis-enclosed section represents a regex capture group used by `substitution` or `ldapQuery`. | `"(.+)ENGINEERING"` `"(.+)DBA"` | | `substitution` | An LDAP distinguished name (DN) formatting template that converts the authentication name matched by the `match` regex into a LDAP DN. Each curly bracket-enclosed numeric value is replaced by the corresponding [regex capture group](http://www.regular-expressions.info/refcapture.html) extracted from the authentication username via the `match` regex. The result of the substitution must be an [RFC4514](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc4514.txt) escaped string. | `"cn={0},ou=engineering, dc=example,dc=com"` | | `ldapQuery` | A LDAP query formatting template that inserts the authentication name matched by the `match` regex into an LDAP query URI encoded respecting RFC4515 and RFC4516. Each curly bracket-enclosed numeric value is replaced by the corresponding [regex capture group](http://www.regular-expressions.info/refcapture.html) extracted from the authentication username via the `match` expression. `mongod` executes the query against the LDAP server to retrieve the LDAP DN for the authenticated user. `mongod` requires exactly one returned result for the transformation to be successful, or `mongod` skips this transformation. | `"ou=engineering,dc=example, dc=com??one?(user={0})"` | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#ldap-authentication-or-authorization-options · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, match, substitution, ldapQuery, "(.+)ENGINEERING", "(.+)DBA"

- [passage] The `{ metacritic : { $ne : null } }` query matches documents where the `metacritic` field exists **and** has a non-null value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#non-equality-filter · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, { metacritic : { $ne : null } }, metacritic
- [passage] The `{ a: { $ne: null } }` query returns the complement, which is every document that `{ a: null }` does not match. The query matches the documents with `_id` values `2`, `3`, `5`, and `6`, including the document that holds an empty array. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#equality-on-an-array-field · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, { a: { $ne: null } }, { a: null }, _id, , , , and 
- [passage] The `{ "a.b": { $ne: null } }` query returns the complement, which is every document that `{ "a.b": null }` does not match: the documents with `_id` values `2`, `3`, `4`, and `5`. That result is not the same as the set of documents that have a non-null value for `a.b`. Neither `_id: 2` nor `_id: 3` has any value at `a.b`, yet the `{ $ne: null }` filter still matches them. A `{ $ne: null }` filter on a dotted path does not necessarily return the same documents as an [`$exists`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#mongodb-query-op.-exists) check on that path. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-for-null-fields.md#equality-on-a-dotted-path · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, { "a.b": { $ne: null } }, { "a.b": null }, _id, , , , and

- [passage] - Inequality operators such as [`$ne`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/ne.md#mongodb-query-op.-ne) or [`$nin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nin.md#mongodb-query-op.-nin) are range operators, not equality operators. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md#additional-considerations · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $ne, $nin
- [passage] The second [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match) stage uses `$rand` in a match expression to further refine the selection. For each document, `$rand` generates a value between 0 and 1. The threshold of `0.5` in the less than [`($lt)`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lt.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-lt) comparison means that [`$expr`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#mongodb-query-op.-expr) will be true for about half the documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/rand.md#select-random-items-from-a-collection · keywords: query operator anti-pattern, $match, $rand, 0.5, ($lt), $expr
